memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You are to buy from your own people on the basis of the number of years
since the Jubilee. And they are to sell to you on the basis of the number
of years left for harvesting crops. When the years are many, you are to
increase the price, and when the years are few, you are to decrease the
price, because what is really being sold to you is the number of crops'"
- Lev 25:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is remarkably practical. The price of land depended on how many years
of harvest remained before the next Jubilee. Everyone knew the reset was
coming, so they priced accordingly. The future shaped the present
transaction.

That is a wise way to live. What you know about the future should shape
how you act now.

Dear reader, we believers know something about the future too. We know
that this present order is temporary, that Christ will return, and that we
will each give an account (2 Cor 5:10). If we truly believed it, it would
shape how we spend, save, work and treat people today.

Jesus told us to store up treasures in heaven, where moth and rust do not
destroy (Matt 6:20). Paul said the time is short, so those who buy
something should live as if it were not theirs to keep (1 Cor 7:29-31).

This is not about becoming impractical or careless. The Israelite still did
real business with real prices. It is about doing so with eternity in
view.

An approaching Jubilee changed the price of a field. An approaching
eternity should change the shape of a life. Let what is coming shape what
you do today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does the reality of eternity actually shape my daily choices?
2. Where am I investing as though this life is all there is?
3. What treasure am I storing up in heaven?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, help me live today in the light of eternity. Let what is coming
shape how I spend my time, money and love right now. Amen.
